title: The Call to Settle Badr’s Account • A Dream, a Counsel • Three Hundred Turned Back on the Road • Those Whose Help Was Not Accepted • Fifty on the Mountain • The Right of the Sword • Hamzah’s Spear, Wahshi’s Spear • The One Whom the Angels Washed • The Pass Left Empty

blocks.0: The Call to Settle Badr’s Account
blocks.1: At Badr seventy of Makkah died. Seventy went to Madinah as captives. In every house of Makkah there was now an empty place. Some had no father, some no brother, some no son. Abu Sufyan’s caravan had returned safely, and the profit of that trade was lying deposited in Makkah. ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi‘ah, ‘Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl and Safwan ibn Umayyah went to Abu Sufyan and the other owners of the caravan. They said, Muhammad has killed our best. With this wealth help us fight him, perhaps we can take revenge. They agreed. The call spread. The Ahabish, Kinanah and the tribes of Tihamah joined too.{{1}}
blocks.2: One was Abu ‘Izzah. A poet. He had been captured at Badr, and the Prophet {{1}} had shown him mercy and released him. He was poor, the father of many daughters. Safwan said to him, help us with your poetry. Abu ‘Izzah said, Muhammad has been kind to me. Safwan said, if you return I will take responsibility for your daughters, and if you die they will live with my daughters. He went. He went around from tribe to tribe, reciting poetry.{{2}}
blocks.3: Another had a task. Jubayr ibn Mut‘im had an Abyssinian slave, Wahshi. Expert at throwing the spear, almost never missing. Jubayr said, if you kill Muhammad’s uncle Hamzah (RA) and take revenge for my uncle Tu‘aymah, you are free. Quraysh set out with three thousand, with two hundred horses. Some women went along, so that the fighters would not think of fleeing. With Abu Sufyan was Hind bint ‘Utbah, whose father and brother had died at Badr. When she passed by Wahshi, Hind would say, Abu Dasmah, calm our insides, and calm yourself too.{{1}}
blocks.4: Badr had broken their hands. From a broken hand hatred spreads, and stubbornness too. That stubbornness became capital, became an army, became song. When revenge falls into a merchant’s hand it becomes investment capital. In our homes too, pouring money into lawsuits and old quarrels, years go by. But an investment whose very name is hatred never yields a profit.
blocks.6: Quraysh came and camped near Uhud. News reached Madinah. That night the Prophet {{1}} saw a dream.
blocks.8: I saw in a dream that I shook a sword, and its tip broke off. That was the loss the believers suffered on the day of Uhud. Then I shook it again, and it became better than before. That was the victory Allah brought and the gathering of the believers. And I saw cattle there too, and whatever Allah does is good; those cattle were the believers on the day of Uhud.{{1}}
blocks.9: The dream also had a strong coat of mail. That coat of mail was Madinah. And cattle being slaughtered. Those cattle were some of the Companions.{{1}}
blocks.10: So his view was to fight staying in Madinah. Let the women and children go to the fortresses, the fighting will be in the lanes, arrows shot from the rooftops. Madinah had by then blocked up its lanes and made them a fortress. ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy’s view was the same. But many of the Companions, who had not been able to be at Badr, wanted to go out and fight. The honour of Badr had slipped from their hands, so they were restless for another chance. Hamzah (RA) said, by the One who sent down the Book upon you, we will fight them, and we will not sit in Madinah. Nu‘aym ibn Malik (RA) said, Prophet of Allah, do not deprive us of Paradise. By the One in whose hand is my soul, I will enter Paradise. The Prophet {{1}} said, by what strength? He said, I love Allah and His Messenger, and I will not flee from the battlefield. The Prophet {{2}} said, you have spoken the truth. He was martyred that very day.{{3}}
blocks.11: The middle of the month of Shawwal, a Friday. The Prophet {{1}} prayed the Jumu‘ah prayer, gave counsel, told them to be patient. That very day a man of Banu al-Najjar, Malik ibn ‘Amr (RA), had died. The Prophet {{2}} first prayed his funeral prayer. Then he went into his house and put on his coat of mail. Now many of the Companions realized the Prophet’s {{3}} view was actually to stay. They said, O Messenger of Allah, if you wish, we will stay. The Prophet {{4}} said, it is not fitting for a prophet, after he has put on his coat of mail, before Allah has decided between him and the enemy, to take it off.{{5}}
blocks.12: Counsel was sought. Differing views came. The Prophet {{1}} set aside his own view and accepted the view of many. Then once the decision was made, there was no question of going back. In our homes too there is counsel. But after a decision is made we become of two kinds. Some keep lamenting, I did say so. Some, having given a differing view in the counsel, take it as a personal insult. After the counsel of Uhud, there was no disagreement left among the Companions. What the Prophet {{2}} decided became everyone’s.
blocks.14: (O Prophet! Recall that time of the Battle of Uhud) when in the morning you went out from your home to position the believers at their posts for battle. And Allah hears everything and knows everything.{{1}}
blocks.15: Three Hundred Turned Back on the Road
blocks.16: With a thousand Companions the Prophet {{1}} set out from Madinah, taking the road called Badi‘. Ibn Umm Maktum (RA) was left in charge of prayer in Madinah. Reaching a place called al-Shawt, between Uhud and Madinah, ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy stopped. He said, Muhammad did not listen to me, he listened to those boys. Why should we get ourselves killed? He turned back with three hundred men. After them went ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn Haram (RA), the father of Jabir (RA). He said, do not leave your people and the Prophet in front of the enemy. They said, if we knew there would be fighting, we would not have turned back. ‘Abdullah said, may Allah keep you away, enemies of Allah. Allah will make His Prophet independent of you.{{2}}
blocks.17: On one side, the Companions then had two views. One group said, fight them, they are hypocrites. The other group said, no.
blocks.19: When the Prophet {{1}} set out for Uhud, some of those who had set out with him turned back. The Companions became two groups. One group said, we will fight them. The other said, we will not fight. Then it was revealed: ‘What is the matter with you that you have become two groups concerning the hypocrites?’{{2}}
blocks.20: Within the army two tribes also grew weak. Banu Salimah and Banu Harithah. The thought of turning back came to them too. Allah held them firm.
blocks.22: Two groups among you were thinking that they had lost heart. Yet Allah was their guardian and helper. The believers should rely on Allah alone.{{1}}
blocks.23: This verse is about those two tribes. Jabir (RA) used to say, it was revealed about us. And I would not want it not to have been revealed, because Allah said in it, ‘Allah is their guardian’.{{1}}
blocks.24: Jabir (RA) was happy even though he knew his own weakness was recorded in the Qur’an. Because in the same verse Allah’s guardianship is also recorded. We want to hide our mistakes. For those whose mistakes too are written in history, beside their mistakes the announcement of Allah’s forgiveness is also written. However much we may break down on one day, for the one whose guardian is Allah, that is not the last word.
blocks.25: Those Whose Help Was Not Accepted
blocks.26: The Prophet {{1}} was going around looking over the soldiers of the camp. There were some boys, who were young in age. One of them was ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (RA), who later used to say himself,
blocks.28: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} presented me for fighting on the day of Uhud. I was fourteen then. He did not permit me. On the day of al-Khandaq he presented me. I was fifteen then. He permitted me.{{2}}
blocks.29: With him others also went back: Usamah ibn Zayd, Zayd ibn Thabit, al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA), Usayd ibn Zuhayr, ‘Arabah ibn Aws. They too had to go back. Rafi‘ ibn Khadij was also small. But he could shoot arrows, so he got permission. Samurah ibn Jundub was small, and was being left out. He said, I can beat Rafi‘ in wrestling. A wrestling match took place. Samurah won. He too got permission.{{1}}
blocks.30: The Ansar tribes of Madinah were bound by treaty with the Jews. They asked the Prophet {{1}}, shall we call our allies the Jews for help? The Prophet {{2}} said, we have no need of them.{{3}}
blocks.31: Yet that day one of the Jews entered the fight. Mukhayriq. A Jew of Banu Tha‘labah. He said, O Jews, you know that helping Muhammad is your duty. They said, but today is Saturday. He said, you have no Saturday. He took his sword and weapons and said, if I am killed, all my wealth belongs to Muhammad, he may do with it as he wishes. Then he went to the field and died fighting. The Prophet {{1}} said, Mukhayriq is the best of the Jews. His seven gardens the Prophet {{2}} made a waqf in the way of Allah. The first waqf of Madinah.{{3}}
blocks.32: The help of the one who was a believer was not needed. And the one who was of another religion suddenly offered his own chest. Whose side a person is really on, in the end that is recognized on the battlefield. Not by looking at the label.
blocks.34: Seven hundred Companions reached near Uhud. Ahead a high mountain, below it a flat field. On the other side the Quraysh army stood in rows. The Prophet {{1}} arranged the troops with their backs to the mountain, so that no one could attack from behind. He told the soldiers, no one will begin the fight unless I say so. Right behind the Muslim army was a mountain pass. Through that very pass the enemy’s horsemen could come and pounce from behind. Fifty archers were stationed there. Their leader was ‘Abdullah ibn Jubayr (RA).
blocks.36: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} stationed a group of archers and appointed ‘Abdullah as their commander over them. He said, do not leave your place. If you see us victorious over the enemy, still do not leave your place. And if you see them victorious over us, even then do not come to help us.{{2}}
blocks.37: Not even if we win, not even if we lose. Whatever happens, this place must not be left. The Prophet {{1}} gave the banner into the hand of Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA). He put on two coats of mail. On the other side, on the right wing of Quraysh’s horsemen was Khalid ibn al-Walid, on the left ‘Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl.{{2}}
blocks.39: Taking a sword in his hand the Prophet {{1}} called out.
blocks.41: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} took a sword on the day of Uhud. He said, who will take this from my hand? Everyone stretched out their hands. Each was saying, I, I. He said, who will take it with its right? Then everyone held back. Simak ibn Kharashah Abu Dujanah (RA) said, I will take it with its right. He took it and with it split open the heads of the polytheists.{{2}}
blocks.42: Every hand reached out. But hearing ‘its right’ everyone stopped. Because right means duty. Asking for a sword is easy. Bearing its duty is hard. What is that right? In Ibn Ishaq’s narration, the Prophet {{1}} said, strike the enemy with it until it bends. Abu Dujanah (RA) tied a red band on his head, which, when worn, everyone knew meant today he had made up his mind to die. With the band tied he began to strut proudly between the two lines. The Prophet {{2}} saw him and said, this walk is disliked by Allah, but not in a place like this today.{{3}}
blocks.43: Al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam (RA) felt a little hurt. The Prophet {{1}} had not given it to his cousin, but had given it to Abu Dujanah (RA). He decided, I will see what he does with this sword. He saw that Abu Dujanah (RA) was cutting down whoever he found. One polytheist was finishing off the wounded. Abu Dujanah (RA) went in front of him and finished him. Then he raised the sword over the head of a woman. That was Hind. The sword did not come down. He drew back. He said, I will not use the sword of the Messenger of Allah on a woman. Al-Zubayr (RA) says, I understood, Allah and His Messenger know best.{{2}}
blocks.44: The one who received power first asked, what is its right? We want power, we want position, we want a car, we want a house. Each has a right that comes with it. In front of whom to draw a line, when to stop the hand. And Abu Dujanah (RA) recognized, right in the middle of valour, where the sword must be lowered. Even in front of one woman of the enemy.
blocks.46: The fight began. The Muslims began to advance. Hamzah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib (RA) plunged like lightning into the disbelievers. ‘Uthman, son of the standard-bearer Talhah ibn Abi Talhah, fell into his hands. Then more standard-bearers. Siba‘ ibn ‘Abd al-‘Uzza came out. Hamzah (RA) said to him, are you opposing Allah and His Messenger? Then he struck, and Siba‘ was wiped out like yesterday. But behind a rock Wahshi was waiting then.
blocks.48: I was the slave of Jubayr ibn Mut‘im. At Badr Hamzah (RA) had killed Tu‘aymah. So Jubayr said to me, if you kill Hamzah (RA) and take revenge for my uncle, you are free. ... I hid for Hamzah (RA) under a rock. When he came near I threw my spear. The spear went in below his navel and came out between his two hips. That was my last meeting with him.{{1}}
blocks.49: The lion was finished. The one who knew no fear, a slave brought him down from behind. Hamzah (RA) was martyred. The Prophet’s {{1}} uncle, his milk-brother.{{2}}
blocks.50: That Wahshi returned to Makkah and was freed. Then Makkah was conquered, he fled to Ta’if. When the delegation of Ta’if decided to go to the Prophet {{1}}, he had nowhere left to go. Someone said, he does not kill anyone who accepts Islam.
blocks.52: I went and stood before the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. He saw me and said, are you Wahshi? I said, yes. He said, did you kill Hamzah (RA)? I said, it was as the news that reached you says. He said, can you keep your face hidden from me? I went out.{{2}}
blocks.53: In the shade of Islam Wahshi (RA) was spared. But the Prophet {{1}} did not want to see his face in front of him. Forgiving someone is one thing. Sitting with a smiling face while seeing their face in front of you is another. The Prophet {{2}} kept the difference between the two. He accepted Islam, and did not hide the wound in his own chest. Some forgiveness takes place in the heart but does not climb into the house. Slowly that too becomes easy. Knowing how to give oneself that time is another greatness of a person. There was another chapter in Wahshi’s life. After the passing of the Prophet {{3}}, Musaylimah the Liar emerged. Wahshi (RA) said, I will go out, perhaps by killing him I can make amends for the killing of Hamzah (RA). In the Battle of Yamamah he threw that same spear. Musaylimah died. An Ansari had also struck with his sword.{{4}}
blocks.54: Wahshi (RA) later used to say, I killed the best of people, and also the worst. Our sins do not leave us. But if someone truly returns, Allah’s door is open for them too.
blocks.55: The One Whom the Angels Washed
blocks.56: That day another had entered among the polytheists. Hanzalah ibn Abi ‘Amir (RA). His father was Abu ‘Amir al-Rahib. In the Jahiliyyah everyone called him the monk, because of his worship. But when Islam came he did not recognize the truth, did not want to recognize it. The Prophet {{1}} gave him the name, the sinner. He had left Madinah and gone off with Quraysh. And the son stood with the Prophet {{2}}. Hanzalah (RA) went straight toward Abu Sufyan. He threw him to the ground, raised his sword. Then Shaddad ibn Aws saw that. He struck. Hanzalah was martyred. After the battle the Prophet {{3}} said, the angels are washing your companion. Go to his wife and ask what the matter is. His wife said, as soon as the call to battle reached his ears, he went out. At that time he was in a state of impurity. The Prophet {{4}} said, that is why the angels washed him.{{5}}
blocks.57: His name remained, Ghasil al-Mala’ikah. The one whom the angels washed. The morning after the wedding night. A new wife at home. Yet leaving on hearing the call. So quickly that even the time for a bath was not taken. When a call comes to us, what do we do? Hearing the adhan we sit, saying there is work. Hanzalah’s hand held a wedding morning. Before one call Hanzalah kept no reckoning. The angels washed him.
blocks.59: The first part of the fight belonged to the Muslims. The polytheists began to flee. Al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam (RA) says, I saw Hind and her companion women running with their shanks bared. Spoils of war were coming into the Muslims’ hands. The tents, weapons, camels left behind by the fleeing enemy. Then the archers standing on the mountain looked on.
blocks.61: When we met them, they fled, until I saw the women running up the mountain, they had lifted their garments from their shanks, their anklets showing. Then the archers began to say, the spoils, the spoils! ‘Abdullah said, the Prophet {{1}} took a pledge from me, that you would not leave your place. They refused. When they refused, their faces were turned away, and seventy were killed.{{2}}
blocks.62: Except ‘Abdullah ibn Jubayr (RA) and a few others, almost all went down. Their argument was, the Prophet {{1}} had said it for that time, for as long as the fighting was going on. The fight had already been won. Did the Prophet’s {{2}} command really have any word about time? The command was, even if you see us winning, do not leave. Khalid ibn al-Walid saw the mountain pass empty. He circled around and came up over it. ‘Abdullah and a few of his companions fought to the end and were martyred.{{3}}
blocks.63: What happened next turned the joy of victory into terror in a moment. Horsemen from above, the fugitives came back from the front. The Muslims were surrounded on both sides. Just then someone cried out.
blocks.65: On the day of Uhud the polytheists were defeated. Then Iblis cried out, servants of Allah, behind you! So the front group came back and began fighting the group behind. Hudhayfah (RA) saw his father Yaman (RA). He said, servants of Allah, my father, my father! ‘A’ishah (RA) says, by Allah, they did not stop, they killed him. Hudhayfah (RA) said, may Allah forgive you. ‘Urwah says, by Allah, a goodness remained in Hudhayfah (RA) until death.{{1}}
blocks.66: Yaman (RA) and Thabit ibn Waqash (RA) were very old. So they had been left in the fortress with the women. But hearing of the fight they said, only a little of our life remains, let us go. They came down into the battle. They fell on the wrong side. Thabit was killed by the polytheists. Yaman (RA) was killed by Muslims themselves, by mistake. What did Hudhayfah (RA) say? He said, may Allah forgive you. He even gave away his father’s blood money as a charity to the Muslims.{{1}}
blocks.67: The mistake happened at the wrong time. The one whose father died forgave in that very moment. When someone’s mistake harms us we remember it for years. Hudhayfah (RA) did not remember. And how small the archers’ mistake was when it began! One argument: the command was actually tied to time. The command had not changed, our interpretation had. The command that goes against my liking, for that we search the hardest for interpretations.

o: Victory and the gathering of the believers

quiz.q: What was the interpretation of the strong coat of mail in the dream?
o: The believers on the day of Uhud

quiz.q: What was the Prophet’s ﷺ own view in the consultation?
o: To go to Uhud and fight
To station the archers on the mountain

quiz.q: After the consultation the Prophet ﷺ put on his coat of mail and then did not change his view. Why?
o: The enemy’s horsemen had been sighted
It is not fitting for a prophet to take off a coat of mail once he has put it on
The archers had already taken their places
quiz.e: Ibn Ishaq and al-Bayhaqi ← Ibn Kathir.

quiz.q: Between Uhud and Madinah, where did ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy stop?
With how many men did ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy turn back?
Who was left in charge of prayer in Madinah?
Which two tribes had grown weak?
At what age was Ibn ‘Umar (RA) turned back on the day of Uhud?
How many archers were stationed at the pass, and who was their commander?
In whose hand was the Muslims’ banner placed?
In which battle did Wahshi (RA), who later accepted Islam, kill Musaylimah?
Which standard-bearer of the polytheist army fell into Hamzah’s (RA) hands?
‘Keep your face away from me’: why did the Prophet ﷺ say this to Wahshi?
o: The Prophet ﷺ did not accept Wahshi’s Islam
Even after forgiveness, seeing the face brings back the grief for the beloved uncle
He wanted to hand Wahshi over to the Companions

quiz.q: Seeing the one who hurt you brings the pain back. From the Prophet’s ﷺ words about Wahshi, what do you learn?
o: After forgiveness, mixing socially is obligatory
Forgiveness and easy mixing are different things
If you forgive, no pain should remain in the heart

quiz.q: What was the Jahiliyyah title of Hanzalah’s (RA) father, and the name the Prophet ﷺ gave him?
In the dars’s analysis, where is the weakness in the argument the archers gave for leaving their place?
o: The command was only for the soldiers of the front row
The command was only for the enemy’s horsemen
The command applied only while the Prophet ﷺ was present
There was no condition of time; even when winning, they could not leave

quiz.q: When someone’s mistake causes you a great loss, what can you say, like Hudhayfah (RA)?
o: ‘I will certainly take revenge for this loss’
